container: The rise of virtual reality is transforming entertainment, education, healthcare, and work. Immersive simulations let students explore distant places, help surgeons practice delicate procedures, and give designers new ways to test ideas. Businesses can train employees safely and connect teams across distance. Yet this technology also raises concerns. Headsets may cause discomfort, isolation, or eye strain, while collecting sensitive data. High costs can limit access, and environments may blur the line between experience and manipulation. As virtual reality grows, thoughtful design, strong privacy protections, and fair access will help ensure its benefits outweigh its risks.
